# Findings

Status: reproduced

## Hypothesis

- add() returns a + b + 1, so every printed sum drifts one too high
- a stdlib-only inline repro reproduces without installing calcbox

## Evidence

- Issue: add() returns a sum that is off by one
- Trigger: call add(2, 3)
- Gate (final): reproduced — matched 1/1 expected symptom entries in stdout

## Research

verdict: likely-regression
- https://example.com/docs/calcbox-add
- https://github.com/demo/calcbox/issues/2

| version | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| 1.1.0 | not-reproduced |
| 1.2.0 | reproduced |

lastGood: 1.1.0
firstBad: 1.2.0

## Fix sketch

Drop the stray `+ 1` in add() so it returns a + b, matching sub() and the documented sum.

## Environment

- Execution: Linux container (this run executed in a Linux container).
- Reported environment (from issue report): Environment: calcbox 1.2.0, stock python3, no dependencies.
